row.problem_statement:
# Bug in map_err method of Ok class

<!-- Summary. -->

I found a bug in the `map_err` method of the `Ok` class in the Result library. When trying to map errors, the method doesn't work correctly for successful results.

<!-- What you expected. -->

I expected the `map_err` method to return the original `Ok` value unchanged when called on an `Ok` result, since there's no error to map.

<!-- What happened instead. -->

Instead, it seems to be returning the operation function itself rather than the original `Ok` value, causing errors when trying to use the result.

```python
from result import Ok, Err

# This works fine
err_result = Err('nay')
mapped_err = err_result.map_err(str.upper)
print(mapped_err.err())  # Prints: 'NAY'

# This fails
ok_result = Ok('yay')
mapped_ok = ok_result.map_err(str.upper)
print(mapped_ok.ok())  # Should print 'yay' but causes an error
```

The issue appears to be in the implementation of the `map_err` method in the `Ok` class. It seems to be returning the operation function instead of returning `self`.
